title: fullcycle skips a declared restore without saying so when the test phase fails after a passing build
body:
Found by critic-shell reviewing the fix for issue `0068` on 2026-09-16, by reading the code. Not reproduced in a run.

`lib/cmd/fullcycle`'s restore half runs only when every phase passed: its gate is `[ "$cleaned" = 1 ] && [ "${#atrisk[@]}" -gt 0 ] && [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]`. A project that declares `commands.fullcycle.restore` precisely so a cycle puts back what it darkens gets no restore when `test rust` fails after `build all` passed, and nothing says the restore was skipped.

The after-half link check does run on that path. It names the dark links and tells the operator to "Rebuild with a RELEASE profile before doing anything else" -- a remedy that does not mention the declared restore at all, in the one estate class that went to the trouble of declaring it.

## Why it is worth an issue

A test failure is no reason to leave the toolchain dark: the build passed, and the restore exists for exactly the case where it passed without repopulating `release/`. The operator is left with dangling binaries and advice to perform by hand what their own config already says how to do.

## Shape of a fix, not a ruling

Gate the restore on a build having passed since the clean -- `rebuilt` in `_fullcycle_run`, added by `0068` -- rather than on the cycle's `rc`, keeping the failing phase's rc as the run's verdict. Or, if a restore after a failed test is judged unsafe, print that the declared restore was skipped and why. Hold it with an arm: test phase fails after a dev-profile build, a watched link is dark, a restore is declared.



## Fixed by vc on 2026-09-16, in 0.1.1 on hv's instruction

hv gave 0070 to vc while dc writes ST0007's design. The fix takes this issue's first shape: **the restore is gated on a build having passed since the clean** (`rebuilt` in `_fullcycle_run`, from 0068), not on the cycle's rc. A test failure after a passing build now runs the declared restore, and with no restore declared the cycle says so. **The failing phase's rc stays the verdict:** a failed restore and the dark-link check both redden a green cycle, and neither replaces the rc of a phase that had already failed. Until now the dark-link check set rc 1 over any earlier failure.

Four arms in `tests/unit/fullcycle.bats`. Three were red first: the restore runs after a failed test and the run keeps rc 101; a failing restore after a failed test leaves rc 101 and names rc 7; an undeclared restore prints `NO RESTORE COMMAND DECLARED`. The fourth guards the other side: a FAILED build never runs the restore. It was green before the fix, because the old gate also blocked that case, and it was added because a mutation dropping the build condition survived the first three. **Four mutations, each red on exactly the expected arms:** the gate back on rc (the three new arms); a restore's rc replacing a failed phase's (arm 2); the dark-link check always setting rc 1 (arm 2); no build condition (arm 4). `fullcycle.bats` 42 of 42; lint clean.
